title.narrative: IDF-Enhancing Institutional and Legal Framework for Environmental Permitting in Belarus

description.narrative: The main activities and (measurable) outputs expected from this IDF grant are described below. i.,,Drafting the program document of the Government on Pollution Prevention and Control in Belarus. ii.,,Establishing the system of the BAT technical guidance notes elaboration, including developing and publishing pilot technical guidance notes for two priority industrial sectors. iii.,,Proposing key legal reform package on environmental permitting system, including procedure rules. iv.,,Conducting an inventory and building electronic data base of installations that fall under the scope of integrated permitting. v.,,Training in integrated environmental permitting for the MEP central office staff, regional (oblast) permitting officials and enterprise environmental managers. vi.,,Conducting stakeholders consultations, information and dissemination campaign. The main outputs will be public hearings and workshops, involving enterprises, industry associations, NGOs, inspectorates, other government stakeholders, publications and promotional materials on the new permitting regime. Likely Outcomes While supporting the Government's request to prepare the legal basis for integrated environmental permitting, this IDF grant is mainly focused on strengthening critical institutional capacity to formulate, implement and monitor modern environmental policies aligned with EU standards. The expected outcomes of this IDF grant also include improvement of investment climate due to streamlined, more predictable and fair business permitting and inspections. TF058127 The grant will facilitate the establishment of the legal and institutional basis for integrated environmental permitting in hopes that the new permitting system will contribute to a reduction in emissions and pollution of the environment.
